topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: Why Bouncing Blocks Count Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students and undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Setup: The Elastic Collision Problem
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
The wall collision reverses the small block.
Momentum and kinetic energy remain conserved.
animations: Create two blocks of masses m1=1, m2=100 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] at #FFFFFF on a #000000 plane.
Highlight mass m2=100 in #FF00FF and m1=1 in #00FFFF.
Show collision between m1 and m2, then wall reflection using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg] for m1.
Flash the collision point in #FF0000 to emphasize momentum transfer.
Show final velocity of m1 as negative and m2 as positive.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Mapping to Velocity Space
lecture_lines: Map velocities as coordinates on a plane.
Wall impacts look like reflections across axes.
Block collisions reflect across a constant line.
animations: Display axes in #FFFFFF for velocity mapping.
Display reflections across axes for [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg], and line for [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] collision.
Highlight reflection vectors in #00FFFF to track velocity changes.

sections.title: The Geometric Connection
lecture_lines: The mass ratio determines the wedge angle.
Increasing mass makes the wedge very narrow.
Reflections bounce back and forth inside.
The number of bounces measures the arc.
It behaves like a bouncing billiard ball.
animations: Construct a wedge with angle theta = arctan(sqrt(m1/m2)) at #FF00FF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billiard.svg].
Animate [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] trajectory bouncing inside the wedge.
Highlight the arc of movement in #00FFFF for clarity.

sections.title: The Grand Reveal: Digits of Pi
lecture_lines: Collision counts follow digits of Pi.
Conservation laws naturally encode the constant Pi.
Physics counting computes the circle's arc.
animations: Simultaneously animate bounce counts for each ratio using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg].
Color matching labels for counts and Pi digits in #00FFFF, layered behind [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/walls.svg].
Flash the final Pi value in #FF00FF to emphasize convergence.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Counting collisions is measuring an angle.
Discrete bounces approximate the circular arc.
Collisions effectively calculate the value of Pi.
animations: Fade in circular arc [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg] with sector angle theta.
Scale the sector highlighting with theta = arctan(sqrt(m1/m2)) in #FF00FF.
Display Pi formula with convergence value in #00FFFF.
